item.title: Datasette Charts plugin updates improve hooks and adds documentation website
item.description:
Datasette Charts plugin updates improve hooks and adds documentation website

The datasette-charts plugin has released an update addressing friction points identified in its chart type plugin hooks, along with the launch of a dedicated documentation website.

🔍 Overview

The datasette-charts plugin features a hook system that allows other plugins to define new chart types. To test this functionality, Claude Opus 5.5 was used to build an experimental plugin, which revealed several friction points in the design. The current release addresses these issues to improve the development process for additional chart plugins.

⚙️ Key details

  • The release improves the ergonomics of building additional chart plugins.
  • Friction points identified by an experimental Claude Opus 5.5 plugin have been resolved.

🚀 Availability

  • A new website for the plugin is available at charts.datasette.io.
  • The website includes a tutorial for plugin authors.
  • A gallery displays core charts and annotations, with each item linking to an interactive demo on Datasette Lite.

#Datasette #Python #DataVisualization #Plugins #AIAssistedDevelopment

Source: Release: datasette-charts 0.4a0

item.title: i-have-adhd plugin provides ADHD-friendly output for coding assistants
item.description:
i-have-adhd plugin provides ADHD-friendly output for coding assistants

The i-have-adhd plugin was released to make AI-powered coding assistants more accessible for users with ADHD. The plugin reformats outputs as numbered action steps, leads with the next action, and avoids unnecessary tangents or pleasantries.

🧩 How it works

The plugin modifies how a coding assistant responds by:

  • Breaking tasks into numbered steps
  • Leading with immediate actions
  • Ending with one concrete next step
  • Making test failures visible
  • Using matter-of-fact error messages

⚙️ Key details

The plugin is available as a skill that can be installed from https://github.com/ayghri/i-have-adhd. Refer to the repo’s AGENTS.md for installation instructions.

Action Command
Uninstall current plugin claude plugin uninstall i-have-adhd
Remove from marketplace claude plugin marketplace remove i-have-adhd
Add forked version claude plugin marketplace add <your-username>/i-have-adhd
Install specific fork claude plugin install i-have-adhd@i-have-adhd

🚀 Availability

The plugin can be installed immediately from the GitHub repository. The instructions require forking, editing skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md, then swapping your copy in.

💡 Why it matters

The approach is loosely based on The Adult ADHD Tool Kit by J. Russell Ramsay and Anthony L. Rostain, but adapted for how an LLM should respond rather than human daily organization. The output is ADHD-friendly—no diagnosis needed—and stops coding agents from burying answers in verbose explanations.

#ADHD #AI-assistant #plugins #accessibility

Source: ayghri/i-have-adhd

item.title: New DSH Plugin Delivers Free Access to Frontier Models Without Login or API Keys
item.description:
New DSH Plugin Delivers Free Access to Frontier Models Without Login or API Keys

🔍 Overview

The plugin installs directly into dsh and activates a free lane to frontier models. Users can access DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3, and other models instantly without creating accounts or managing API keys. The service is completely free with no usage limits.

🧩 How it works

The plugin integrates as a pure mount point requiring no kernel modifications, build steps, or dependencies. It pulls model lists directly from upstream sources and removes unavailable models from the selector based on gateway responses. The plugin handles routing and provides an OpenAI-compatible local forwarding port for integration with other tools.

⚙️ Key details

Available Channels

Channel Source Features
Free lane OpenCode Zen gateway DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Kimi K3, no authentication
Kilo channel Kilo AI public gateway Free models, no account or key required
Aggregated channel 77 provider registries NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, Groq, Cerebras, SambaNova, Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral, Together, Fireworks, SiliconFlow, Nebius, Chutes, Hugging Face, Cloudflare, Z.ai, Kimi, MiniMax, QwenCloud, Bedrock, Vertex, Vercel AI Gateway, Azure OpenAI, FleetRelay, Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp

Account-based Integrations

Ten account channels are pre-enabled: LobsterAI, Qoder (Chinese version), TRAE, Cline, Loomy, Raccoon, MiniMax Code, ZCode, Gemini, and EAC channel from project maintainers.

Additional Features

  • Reasoning control: Models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash expose reasoning level menus (Off/Low/High/Max)
  • Local dashboard: Tracks token usage, speed, and latency with in-device analytics
  • Hot reload: Updates apply immediately without restart
  • Automatic updates: Built-in checker with rollback capability

🚀 Availability

The plugin achieved GitHub Trending #1 and JavaScript weekly trend #1 status. Users can join the OFM technology exchange QQ group (974582805) for support.

item.title: Pi AI-agent Runtime Expands with Pluggable Extension Packages
item.description:
Pi AI-agent Runtime Expands with Pluggable Extension Packages

Pi AI-agent runtime now supports pluggable extension packages that expose LLM-callable tools via MCP, covering workspace integrations, automation, memory, scheduling, and more. These packages enable developers to build composable AI agents using shared TypeScript libraries.

🧩 Available Extensions

The following extension packages are available under the @amaster.ai npm scope:

Package Purpose
@amaster.ai/pi-browser-use Browser automation via chrome-devtools-mcp
@amaster.ai/pi-attachments Attachment normalization, upload handling, document parsing
@amaster.ai/pi-telemetry Runtime traces, TTFT, token/cost accounting
@amaster.ai/pi-task-scheduler Cron-based scheduled task management
@amaster.ai/pi-goal Goal derivation and agent condition monitoring
@amaster.ai/pi-web-access Web search, URL extraction, image search
@amaster.ai/pi-computer-use Cross-platform desktop automation
@amaster.ai/pi-channels Feishu, WeCom, and webhook messaging
@amaster.ai/pi-memory Persistent curated memory injection
@amaster.ai/pi-security Resource-aware security policy engine
@amaster.ai/pi-teamwork Team collaboration and issue management
@amaster.ai/pi-image-gen Image generation via multiple providers
@amaster.ai/pi-video-gen Video model clips and batch rendering
@amaster.ai/pi-lark Lark/Feishu workspace integration
@amaster.ai/pi-wecom WeCom workspace integration
@amaster.ai/pi-dingtalk DingTalk workspace integration

⚙️ Core Packages

Package Purpose
@amaster.ai/pi-shared Shared runtime types and contracts
@amaster.ai/pi-storage JSON-file and MySQL/Prisma persistence adapters

🚀 Key Capabilities

  • Each extension exposes LLM-callable tools via MCP
  • Host applications provide HTTP routing, authentication, and product-specific UI
  • Packages are ESM-only and composable
  • On Pi 0.99+, video, teamwork, and memory tools expose bounded structured results
  • Scripts can consume IDs, memory entries, media paths, and QC metadata
  • Extension packages declare their entry point in the pi.extensions field of package.json

#AIagents #TypeScript #MCP #LLM #Automation #Plugins

Source: TGYD-helige/pi

item.title: Datasette Updates Background Task Management and Client Integration
item.description:
Datasette Updates Background Task Management and Client Integration

Datasette has introduced new capabilities for plugin management and internal client functionality.

⚙️ Key details

  • Plugins can now launch and manage background tasks using the new datasette.add_background_task() method.
  • Datasette has been migrated to httpx2 to enable features such as the internal datasette.client.get() method.

#Datasette #plugins #httpx2

Source: Release: datasette 1.0a40

item.title: Claude Code: AI Coding Assistant Launched for Terminal and IDE
item.description:
Claude Code: AI Coding Assistant Launched for Terminal and IDE

Anthropic has released Claude Code, an agentic coding tool designed to accelerate development workflows. The tool integrates directly into terminals, IDEs, or GitHub via natural language commands.

🔍 Overview

Claude Code understands your codebase to automate routine tasks, explain complex code, and manage git workflows. It operates through natural language instructions in your terminal or IDE, with GitHub integration via @claude mentions.

🧩 Key Features

  • Execute routine coding tasks via natural language
  • Explain complex code sections
  • Handle git workflows through commands
  • Report issues using /bug command
  • Extend functionality via custom plugins

⚙️ Installation

Installation methods include:

Platform Command
MacOS/Linux `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh
Homebrew brew install --cask claude-code
Windows `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1
WinGet winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode
NPM (Deprecated) npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code (deprecated)

Post-installation: Navigate to your project directory and run claude.

🛠️ Plugins

The tool supports plugins that add custom commands and agents. See the plugins directory for documentation on available extensions.

⚖️ Feedback & Privacy

Claude Code collects usage data (code acceptance/rejection, conversation data, and /bug feedback) to improve the tool. Safeguards include:

  • Limited retention of sensitive data
  • Restricted access to user sessions
  • Explicit policy against using feedback for model training

Review full policies in the Commercial Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

🚀 Availability

  • Join the Claude Developers Discord for community support
  • Report issues via /bug or GitHub
  • Consult the setup documentation for troubleshooting

#AI #CodingTools #DeveloperTools #Git #Plugins

Source: anthropics/claude-code
